mechanism.summary: Consume the existing owned caller projection and cached immutable read-only direct-eval blueprint once in the same VM evaluator, avoiding redundant native dispatch/context lookup and environment clones. Preserve projection construction and all existing non-admitted paths. Record a stable weak eval-intrinsic identity per realm to guard this new route.
mechanism.generality: Admission uses direct-eval call provenance, a stable intrinsic function identity, live parser context, and immutable bytecode effects: no declarations, closure/template identity state, nested eval, with, suspension, or binding writes/deletes. It handles every admitted cached source and caller without recognizing source text, function names, paths, benchmark IDs, iteration counts or expected values. Each call obtains current values/cells from the ordinary independent projection; it never consumes the caller own environment or caches values/cells.
semantic_risks: Intrinsic identity must be registered once per realm, remain stable after global eval rebinding, and conservatively reject foreign, bound, Proxy, synthetic-unregistered and dynamic-realm routes.

Cache eligibility and parse context must match the existing native path, including caller strictness, private names, this, super, home object, new.target, arguments and module routing; parameter prologues and with retain old behavior.

Read-only bytecode is not side-effect-free: callbacks can mutate canonical cells, realm bindings and objects or throw. Refresh realm-backed caller slots on both success and failure before using existing call-result handling.
Preserve cold/cache-miss, declaration/write/delete, nested-eval, non-string and indirect-eval paths, argument evaluation order, RegExp object identity, TDZ and evaluation-local state.

The consumed environment must be the already independent owned projection, not caller self.env. Reuse the same evaluator and necessary this initialization; no FrameBindings COW, slot-index cache, empty-frame shortcut or global binding-model change is part of this unit.
